text:
Alex: Heads-up — p99 on host->gpu paths jumped after yesterday's kernel-selector patch, noticed in canary; +18% CPU on preparse stage.
Maria: Seen it too. Traces show most of the extra time in request parsing/token boundary detection, not the kernel ops.
Sam: Confirming profile: flamegraph from a hot pod (canary-2):
```
  40%   parse_request
   9%   tokenize_utf8
  12%   stream_coalesce
  14%   grpc_writev_smallwrites
  25%   kernel_dispatch
```
Alex: Interesting that grpc_writev_smallwrites is 14% — that matches increased syscalls we saw on the host. Any change to batching heuristics or writev behavior in the patch?
Jess: The kernel selector PR added a soft-affinity check that alters batching window heuristics when seq_len distribution is skewed. It shouldn't touch writev directly but can increase fragmentation which forces more small writes.
Kevin: Replaying a request locally with tcpdump shows ~3x more small frames after the change. Looks like streaming-chunk boundaries moved earlier.
Maria: So pipeline: selector nudges decision, which shortens the proto-fragment window -> more chunks emitted -> grpc writev sees more smallwrites -> extra syscall overhead and kernel wakeups.
Sam: Also noticed KV cache hit-rate dipped ~2% at 95th percentile. Possibly because preparse now splits requests at different offsets and kv keys mis-align.
Hao: Can we reproduce with a controlled load? I ran 10k requests of mixed short/long prompts against canary vs baseline. Baseline p99=22ms, canary p99=26ms. CPU flamegraphs match the smallwrite bump.
Alex: Thanks Hao. Can we try toggling the soft-affinity flag off and measure? Patch author's flag is `--selector-soft-affinity=true` default. Turn it off to see if regression reverts.
Jess: Quick experiment on canary-2: rolled with flag=false, two minutes later p99 returned to ~22.5ms. KV hit-rate restored.
Kevin: TL;DR: selector change indirectly hurt host-side streaming chunking and KV alignment.
Maria: Proposed fixes: 1) revert soft-affinity until we implement chunk-aware selector, or 2) keep selector but adjust batching window to prefer coalescing writes, and 3) add kv-key normalization that is chunk-boundary invariant.
Sam: Option 2 sounds lowest disruption. We can add a small hysteresis: if writes per-request > N, extend batching window by 5ms. Also add metric emit for smallwrites ratio.
Hao: I sketched a quick change to the batching config in canary to test hysteresis:
```
batching.window_ms = 2
batching.hysteresis_ms = 5  # when smallwrite_ratio > 0.15
smallwrite.threshold = 512
```
Alex: Good. Can we also add a perf regression alert on smallwrite_ratio > 0.12 for any host pool? Means we detect early.
Jess: I'll open the PR to include the hysteresis and the metric. Will mark the kernel-selector patch as blocked until we have a chunk-aware selector implementation.
InfraBot: Deploy started: canary-2 -> batching-hysteresis-v1 at 6801112245 by Jess.
Kevin: Early numbers after deploy: p99 down to 23ms, smallwrite_ratio halved from 0.18 -> 0.09. KV hit-rate back within 0.5% of baseline.
Maria: Great. Follow-ups:
- Jess: PR for hysteresis + metric (in review)
- Sam/Hao: write unit test for kv-key normalization across chunk splits
- Alex: Add alert + dashboard panel for smallwrite_ratio and chunk_count_per_request
- Kevin: Schedule a perf run across fleet tomorrow 03:00 UTC

Jess: Will post PR link when ready. Also thinking longer-term: we should make selector aware of streaming-boundary cost, not just kernel latency estimate. That means adding an estimator for downstream writev/syscall cost.
Alex: Agreed. For now we keep the hysteresis on and un-block kernel-selector rollout until we have chunk-aware selector in a branch.
Sam: One more note — telemetry shows this regression impacts short prompt-heavy tenants more. Add tenant-level alerting.
Hao: I'll attach the replay scripts to the issue.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Closing this thread after PR merges and a fleet-wide perf run confirms no regressions. :thumbsup:
